correctness.rationale: The primary source gives the exact graph-plane formula Theta(Gamma_B)=C(1-S+sum_i lambda_i B_ii/(1+lambda_i^2))/sqrt(det(I+B^T B)). For equal singular values this becomes a constant plus a scalar multiple of tr(B). The trace inequality bounds the numerator by a function of the singular values b_i. After b_i=tan(theta_i), pairwise angle averaging increases the bound by exactly Q sin^2(v), so the global maximum reduces to b_1=...=b_r=t. The resulting derivative has one positive zero. It is t=lambda in the comass-one regime and t=1/((r-1)lambda) in the supercritical regime. The latter is attained by B=-tI, so no gap remains between upper bound and witness. The symbolic replay verifies all closed-form identities.

Targeted source-specific, equal-singular-value, conformal-linear, reciprocal-slope, and exact-comass searches found no covering statement.

value.rationale: The primary source establishes a sharp phase boundary but leaves the quantitative size of calibration failure unresolved beyond it. Equal singular values are the canonical isotropic family in every rank, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact profile reveals a structural transition in the extremizing plane: the source-scale negative graph is optimal only at the boundary, while the genuinely supercritical optimizer moves to a reciprocal slope. This supplies a benchmark norm and equality witness for future work on the full supercritical comass problem.
